answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, so renewal cannot satisfy the mandated 18% cost cut, and negotiate_terms is foreclosed for now. With the contract lapsing in 14 days and no auto-renew, deferring risks an uncontracted gap at 94% committed volume with zero buffer. The low-cost vendor quote meets the mandate outright, and memory_c2 (verified) indicates prior onboarding with this type of vendor switch was quick and invoicing stayed accurate, which is the key evidence needed to judge whether switching increases delivery risk. I also want to check memory_c3 (second-sourcing) as a lower-risk alternative for the next cycle if switch execution looks shaky. Given the tight timeline and no buffer, I'm treating this as a standard (not full broad) rollout — moving primary supply but with heightened monitoring — rather than a small guarded test, since a partial test wouldn't resolve the expiring-contract deadline in time. I'm flagging downstream risk because full dependence on an unproven-at-this-volume vendor under a zero-buffer line is exactly the kind of single-point-of-failure exposure memory_c3 warns against, even though that memory applies more directly to the second-source path than switching outright.
